title: Los Angeles theatres and the Follies' black pit band
summary: Irma worked at the Burbank Theatre; Lee recalls a black orchestra in the pit of the all-white Follies, where a white dancer was fired for speaking to a musician.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: For instance, when we first came here after I told you about the Apex, and then after I stopped doing that and I started playing music, she used to work downtown at the Burbank Theatre; there was a Burbank Theatre down here on Main Street -- you know, Los Angeles really had a lot of places for people to work in entertainment. That was because, for years and years, now that I recall --the
Follies downtown, there was some black bandleader here; he had the band at the Follies for years, and the Follies was an all white show, and they had this black orchestra in the pit.
And I'm talking about like 1932 and '33, I guess, you know -- '34.
But as late as the - what was it, about 1950, one of the white girls that was dancing down there got fired for speaking to one of the black musicians in the orchestra.
No, because I knew the girl. And she knew Paul Kelsh, and she had a conversation with him, you know, like, 'Nice day' or something, and she got fired for speaking to Paul.
Yeah, well that shows you how unpredictable it ...
